question.text: A listed company with 1.5 lakh shareholders manages its share transfer activities in-house. Under SEBI LODR 2015, what is the company required to do?

answer.text: Continue in-house operations without any additional registration
Register as a Category I RTA with SEBI (combined registrar + transfer agent)
Either register with SEBI as a Category II Share Transfer Agent or appoint a SEBI-registered RTA
Outsource to an external SEBI-registered RTA within 90 days, with no other option permitted

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that where a listed entity's in-house share transfer facility crosses the one lakh holder threshold, the listed entity has two permissible options: (a) register with SEBI as a Category II Share Transfer Agent so that it can continue to run the facility in-house, or (b) appoint a SEBI-registered RTA. The Trap: Treating SEBI registration as the only permitted option misses the second route (appoint a SEBI-registered RTA). Conversely, treating an external RTA appointment as the only option misses the in-house Category II route. Note: Category I covers entities that perform both registrar and transfer agent functions, while Category II covers entities that perform only the transfer agent function -- which is why Category II is the relevant registration when the listed entity keeps the transfer facility in-house.
